text:
josh_l: quick flag - I ran the int8 bringup for rk-lite v2 and see ~1.6% MRR degradation concentrated on mid-length queries (10-30 tokens).

josh_l: same checkpoint, different runtime (int8 quantized kernels via new runtime), and we also tried a new candidate truncation policy (truncate doc to 512 tokens instead of 1024).

mina_s: is the delta top1 or aggregate?

josh_l: top1 drives most of it, top3/top5 less so. suggests first-token or early-context sensitivity.

kevin_w: could be truncation changing candidate order or removing early context. did you compare candidate texts pre/post truncation for a sample?

josh_l: yes - in a random 500-query slice, ~9% of candidates lost the last sentence. examples: "...follow the steps below." -> truncated away.

tara_g: truncating tail shouldn't change top1 if model relies on beginning, unless the ranker uses whole-doc features or position embeddings differ after quantization.

kevin_w: also check tokenizer consistency across conversion path. we had a case where a windows newline \r\n was turned into \n only in one pipeline causing different bpe splits near the doc boundary.

josh_l: good call. I diffed token ids for pairs and found mismatches for ~6% of candidates, mostly where truncation boundary cut inside a multibyte grapheme.

mina_s: truncation + a different normalization during serialization could create off-by-one tokens at the tail. does the quantized runtime use the same tokenizer artifacts?

josh_l: the runtime loads the tok.json from the build, but our serializer also runs NFKC normalization earlier. The new bringup accidentally skipped the serializer normalization for performance.

kevin_w: skipping normalization is risky. small unicode differences can flip subtokenization especially for short spans. can you share a reproducible pair?

josh_l: pasted sample below:
```
orig doc snippet: "Install the plugin — then restart the service."
serialized no-normalize: "Install the plugin —then restart the service."
token ids orig: [101, 5234, 999, ...]
token ids no-normalize: [101, 5234, 3456, ...]  <-- changed around em-dash spacing
```

mina_s: em-dash/spacing often causes diffs. ONNX/int8 sometimes exacerbates because logits are tiny differences become ranking shifts.

ops-bot: CI job rk-int8-verify #210 failed: mrr-regression-check (mid-len slice) - logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/210

josh_l: I ran A/B: keep FP16 runtime but apply truncation and no-normalize -> little to no delta. keep normalize but run int8 -> ~0.6% delta. both together -> 1.6%. so it's multiplicative.

tara_g: that suggests two orthogonal effects: tokenizer parity and quant perturbation. mitigation path: re-enable serializer normalization and adjust truncation boundary to avoid cutting multi-codepoint graphemes. also add a token-parity unit test in rankbench.

kevin_w: agree. also add a small eval slice to CI for mid-length queries that alerts on >0.5% MRR drop.

josh_l: created tickets: RINF-7560 (re-enable normalization + add grapheme-aware truncation), RINF-7561 (rankbench token-parity test), RINF-7562 (mid-len MRR alert slice in CI).

eval-bot: created issue RINF-7560, RINF-7561, RINF-7562.

mina_s: once patches are in, let's re-run int8 smoke on the 50k holdout and the 5K mid-len slice. if all green we can proceed with staged rollout.

josh_l: will push patch for normalization + truncation fix today, target rerun tomorrow morning. thanks for the quick triage.

kevin_w: nice find. formatting and truncation edgecases are so sneaky. :pray:

ops-bot: Note: tagging ops-runbook: "tokenizer_parity_checks" and adding to onboarding checklist for model conversions.
